newsitem.title: USA: Greenspan wants to limit bank nonfinancial assets.
newsitem.headline: Greenspan wants to limit bank nonfinancial assets.

text.p: Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan voiced doubts on Thursday about a proposal to allow financial companies to do 25 percent of their business in non-financial activities.
"It sounds a bit high," he told a House Banking subcommittee. But, he added, "I can't give you an alternative number."
Subcommittee Chairwoman Marge Roukema, a Republican from New Jersey, has proposed a bill that would allow financial companies do a quarter of their business in non-financial activities.

"Instead of arbitrarily picking a number out ot the air, you've got to have a sense of what types of organizations we're thinking of that may move in certain directions," Greenspan said. "You need far more analytical detail."

In his opening testimony to the subcommittee, Greenspan backed allowing financial companies to own a "small basket" of non-financial assets, set as a percentage limit of a firm's total assets or capital.
The chairman made clear though that any approach would be transitory.
"By the year 2015 or so, my suspicion is you will not be able to tell easily the distinction between what is a financial institution, what is a bank, what is a non-financial institution," he said.

"So we should recognize that whatever it is that we do, we should not hold back what is the inevitable technological changes that are going to blur the line of all the various aspects of what types of institutions we have," he added.
